ar_psychology_wall.blurb: Psychology Wall is the opening cliff along the trail into Area 51, in the Bigfoot Hollow zone of the eastern Boston Mountains in northwest Arkansas. It holds eleven climbs, mostly bolted sport lines with a couple of trad leads. Grades begin in the 5.7 range, with a handful of 5.8s and a 5.9, then climb through the 5.10s and 5.11 to one hard 5.13 at the top end. The short walk from the car makes it an easy first stop, and its easier lines suit climbers warming up before heading deeper into the hollow.

ar_land_of_the_little_people.blurb: Land of the Little People is a small pocket of the Invasion Area in the Cowell and Deer climbing zone of north-central Arkansas. Nearly all of the eleven climbs, a split of six sport and five trad lines, are found on one freestanding block that stands up to about 65 feet on its tallest side. Grades are easy at the bottom end with a 5.5, then cluster around 5.8 to 5.10, and top out at one 5.12. The surrounding Invasion Area is known for steep, hard climbing, so this block offers a gentler grade range than its neighbours.

ar_crag_central.blurb: Crag Central is one of the cliff sections within the Mount Magazine Proper climbing area of Mount Magazine State Park in western Arkansas. Eleven routes, a mix of six sport and five trad, are spread over a spread of grades: a few moderates from 5.7 to 5.9, a couple of 5.10s, and a good block of 5.11 sport lines, with one 5.12 at the top. A standout is an overhanging 5.9+ trad line along the arete. The wider park is described as a sunny, wind-sheltered spot that works well for winter climbing, though its trails are thorny.

ct_lantern_hill.blurb: Lantern Hill is a small quartzite hill in the North Stonington and Ledyard area of southeastern Connecticut, close to the Rhode Island line. Most of the climbing is on the clean, white southwest cliffs, roughly 30 to 70 feet high, with juggy, vertical to slightly overhanging lines on cracks, arêtes and faces. Eleven climbs are known: six are top-rope and five trad, and grades run from very easy up through the 5.10s, with most in the 5.8 to 5.10 band. Setting top-rope anchors means walking to the summit, so bring long webbing or static line. The east side has noticeably looser rock.

ct_laurel_queen_boulder.blurb: Laurel Queen Boulder is a large glacial erratic in the Burr Pond State Park and Paugnut State Forest boulder fields of northwest Connecticut. It stands about 15 to 20 feet tall, a bit taller on the downhill side, with big solid flakes, cracks, mostly blank faces and an overhanging section, all in pink granitic gneiss. Eleven problems range from V0 and V1 warm-ups through V2 and V3 classics to a couple of V7s. Landings are reported as good, and the boulder sits only a short way off a mountain bike trail within the park's wider collection of several hundred boulders.
